tables.purpose: Stores information about each marketing campaign, including its name, channel, schedule, budget, and current status.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for each marketing campaign.
Descriptive name of the campaign.
Marketing channel used for the campaign (e.g., social_media, affiliate, paid_search).
Date when the campaign started or is scheduled to start.
Date when the campaign ended or is scheduled to end; may be null for ongoing or unscheduled campaigns.
Monetary amount allocated for the campaign.
Current lifecycle state of the campaign (e.g., active, paused, completed).

tables.business_value: Enables reporting on which campaigns have been run, their budgets, channels, and whether they are active, paused, or completed, supporting performance and spend analysis.

ambiguity_flags.note: Currency of the monetary amount is not specified.
Exact definitions of status values (active, paused, completed) are not described.
Null may indicate an ongoing campaign or a campaign with no scheduled end; intent is unclear.

tables.purpose: Stores basic information about each customer, including contact details, sign‑up date, location, and business‑defined classifications of segment and status.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for each customer.
Customer's email address used for contact and identification.
Customer's given (first) name; may be null.
Customer's family (last) name; may be null.
Date the customer record was created or the customer signed up.
Country where the customer is located.
Business‑defined grouping of customers (e.g., new, at_risk, regular, high_value).
Current relationship state of the customer (e.g., active, inactive, churned).

tables.business_value: Enables analysis of the customer base by geography, acquisition date, segment, and activity status, supporting targeting, retention, and churn monitoring.

ambiguity_flags.note: Exact criteria that place a customer into a segment are not evident from the data.
Definitions of status values (active, inactive, churned) are not described.
Future dates appear (e.g., 2025‑08‑26); it is unclear whether this column represents planned sign‑ups or data entry errors.

tables.purpose: Records each sales order placed by a customer, capturing when it occurred, how it was placed, its current processing state, and the monetary total.

column_meanings.meaning: System‑generated unique identifier for the order record.
Reference to the customer who placed the order (links to customers.customer_id).
Date and time when the order was created or processed.
Current lifecycle state of the order (e.g., cancelled, refunded, etc.).
Medium through which the order was received (e.g., in_store, marketplace, mobile_app).
Monetary value of the order total.

tables.relationships: orders.customer_id → customers.customer_id (many‑to‑one relationship linking each order to the customer who placed it).
tables.business_value: Enables analysis of sales volume, order outcomes, and channel performance, supporting revenue tracking and operational reporting.

ambiguity_flags.note: Possible values observed are 'cancelled' and 'refunded'; full set of status codes and their meanings are not documented.
Observed values include 'in_store', 'marketplace', 'mobile_app'; the complete list of channels and their definitions are unknown.
Currency of the monetary amount is not specified.
Column is nullable; unclear whether null indicates missing data, future orders, or other special cases.

tables.purpose: Stores each line item belonging to a sales order, linking the order to a product and capturing how many units were ordered and the price per unit.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for the line item record.
Reference to the order that this line item belongs to (FK to orders.order_id).
Reference to the product being purchased (FK to products.product_id).
Number of units of the product included in this line item.
Price per single unit of the product at the time of the order.

tables.business_value: Enables analysis of what products are sold in each order, quantities sold, and revenue per product, supporting sales performance and inventory planning.

ambiguity_flags.note: Column is nullable; unclear why a line item might exist without an associated order.
Column is nullable; unclear why a line item might exist without a linked product.
Nullable quantity could indicate missing data or optional line items; reason not evident.
Currency of the monetary amount is not specified; also unclear whether price includes tax or discounts.

tables.purpose: Stores each product’s identifying information, its category, price and current availability status.

column_meanings.meaning: System-generated unique identifier for the product.
Descriptive name of the product.
Business-defined grouping or segment the product belongs to.
Monetary price of the product (currency not indicated).
Current availability status of the product (e.g., active, discontinued, out_of_stock).

tables.business_value: Enables reporting on what products exist, how they are priced and categorized, and which are currently sellable, supporting inventory and sales analysis.

ambiguity_flags.note: Currency of the price amount is not specified.
Exact meanings of status values (active, discontinued, out_of_stock) are not described.
